author: Francesco Mattana
title: Pesto Al Cavolo Nero - Tuscan Kale Pesto
ingredients: 1 small garlic clove, or ½ clove for a milder flavour
80-100ml extra virgin olive oil, plus extra if needed
Fine sea salt & freshly ground black pepper
notes: It's best to eat the pesto immediately or the next day. Or transfer it to a clean and sterilised jar, cover the surface with a thin layer of olive oil and refrigerate it for up to 5 days.
instructions_list: Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and meanwhile tear the stems out of the cavolo and discard.
Add the cavolo nero to the boiling water and blanch for 3 minutes, until the leaves are tender but still retain their deep green colour. Drain well and leave to cool slightly.

Add the walnuts, almonds, garlic, grated Grana Padano cheese and anchovies, if using, to a food processor. Add the cavolo nero and a generous pinch of black pepper, then pulse a few times until roughly chopped.

Pour in the olive oil and blitz it until it combines all together. After adding the first 80ml of olive oil if it is still very thick, add a few tbsp of ice cold water and blitz again until you have a thick, creamy pesto.
Taste and season with salt but remember that the Grana Padano and anchovies will already add some saltiness, so season gradually.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente. When the pasta is fully cooked, add it to a bowl with a drizzle of olive oil. Add the pesto to the pasta with a ladle of pasta water. Give it a good stir all together and serve.
description: Cavolo nero or Tuscan kale is a staple in Tuscan cuisine and you will find it in many of their regional dishes. One of my favourite way to cook with it is making a delicious, seasonal, vibrant pesto!It's so good for you, it's packed with essential vitamins, minerals and fibre and it gives the pesto a deep, earthy flavour. You can also add a few anchovies in the pesto if you like for an extra layer of savouriness. You can use the pesto however you prefer, from a simple bruschetta to pasta, risotto - you name it! I served mine with trenette, a pasta shape similar to linguine.
